notes.meaning: Paul introduces himself as a servant, or bond-slave, devoted completely to Jesus Christ. God called him directly to be an apostle, which means a special messenger sent with authority to share the gospel—the good news of God's salvation. Paul did not invent this message, but was set apart by God to proclaim it.

Paul explains that this good news is not a brand-new message or a sudden change in God's plan. God promised it long ago through the Old Testament prophets in the Holy Scriptures. The ancient promises and their fulfillment in Christ confirm and strengthen each other.

The center of the gospel message is God's Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. In his earthly life as a real human being, Jesus was born into the family line of King David. This fulfilled the ancient promises that Israel's Messiah and king would come from David's lineage.

While Jesus lived as a humble man on earth, his rising from the dead openly showed his true power as the Son of God. The Holy Spirit displayed divine power through the resurrection, proving Jesus to be who he claimed to be. The resurrection serves as the firm foundation of Christian faith.

differ.view: Christ was appointed or inaugurated as the Son of God in power at His resurrection regarding His office in salvation history, rather than gaining divinity He did not previously possess.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Verses 3 and 4 may preserve an early Christian confession or creed that existed before Paul wrote this letter.

notes.meaning: Through Jesus, Paul received God's undeserved kindness and the special calling to be an apostle. His mission was to bring people among all the Gentile, or non-Jewish, nations to trust and obey Christ. True faith in Jesus always leads to an obedient life that honors his name.

Paul reminds the Christians living in Rome that they are included in this worldwide calling. They too have been invited by the gospel to belong entirely to Jesus Christ. Because they are Christ's people, Paul writes to them with genuine care and apostolic authority.

Paul greets all the believers in Rome as people dearly loved by God and called to be saints, meaning people set apart as holy to the Lord. He blesses them with grace, which is God's free and unearned favor, and peace through Christ's cross. Both of these spiritual gifts come directly from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

Paul begins by thanking his God through Jesus Christ for all the believers in Rome. Because Rome was the capital of the empire, people traveled there constantly and carried news of the church's faith to other lands. Their faithful testimony became an encouragement to Christians across the known world.

Paul calls God as his witness to show that he is speaking the honest truth. He serves God with his whole heart and spirit by preaching the good news about his Son. Because of that sincere love, Paul never forgets to pray for the Roman church.

In his daily prayers, Paul repeatedly asked God to grant him the chance to visit Rome at last. He had wanted to go for a long time, but he submitted all his travel plans to God's guiding will. He knew that only God's providence could make his journey safe and successful.

Paul eagerly desired to visit the Roman Christians in person so he could share some spiritual blessing or teaching with them. He did not mean performing miracles, but helping them grow spiritually through his preaching and care. His goal was to make them firm and unshakable in their faith.

Paul humbly explains that he does not view himself as superior to the believers in Rome. He looks forward to a shared encouragement where both he and they are strengthened by seeing one another's faith. Even an experienced apostle can be comforted and built up by fellow believers.

Paul wants the believers to know that he had made plans many times to come to Rome. Up to this point, other ministry duties had held him back from making the trip. He wanted to see spiritual fruit and new converts among them, just as he had seen in other Gentile lands.

Paul felt a personal duty and debt to preach the gospel to every group of people. This debt included educated Greeks, uneducated non-Greeks, the cultured scholar, and the ordinary worker. Because God had commissioned him to be the apostle to the Gentiles, he owed the message of Christ to everyone.

Because of this divine obligation, Paul was eager to preach the good news in the city of Rome as well. Rome was the powerful center of the ancient world, but Paul did not shrink back in fear. As much as it was up to him, he stood ready to preach whenever God opened the way.

Paul boldly declares that he is not ashamed of the gospel of Christ. Even though many people mocked the cross as weak and foolish, it is actually God's mighty power to save anyone who trusts in Jesus. This gift of salvation was offered first to the Jewish people and is now offered to Gentiles as well.

The gospel reveals the righteousness of God, which is his way of putting guilty sinners into right standing with himself. This status is received purely through faith from beginning to end, not by earning it through good deeds. Paul confirms this from the prophet Habakkuk, who wrote that the person made right with God will live by faith.

differ.view: God's righteousness is Christ's perfect obedience credited to the believer once and for all through faith alone.
The righteousness of God refers to God's gracious method of saving sinners, leading people from the faith of the Old Testament to the faith of the New.

notes.meaning: Alongside the gospel, God's holy anger is revealed from heaven against all human godlessness and wickedness. God's wrath is not a sudden loss of temper, but his steady and righteous opposition to sin. Sinful people deliberately push down and hide the truth about God so they can keep doing what is evil.

God is entirely fair to judge human rebellion because basic truths about him are clear to everyone. God has placed this understanding inside human hearts and displayed it plainly before their eyes. No one can truthfully say that God kept himself hidden.

Ever since the world was created, God's invisible attributes, such as his eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly visible in the things he made. Anyone who looks at the beauty and order of creation can know that an almighty Creator exists. Because God has provided this clear evidence, people have no valid excuse for ignoring him.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: God can be known with certainty by natural human reason through the visible things he has made in creation.

notes.meaning: Even though people knew about God from what was made, they refused to honor him as God or thank him for his care. Instead, their thinking turned empty and useless as they chased their own false ideas. Because they rejected the light, their foolish hearts fell into deep spiritual darkness.

People bragged about their cleverness and claimed to be deeply wise philosophers. In reality, turning away from the true God turned them into complete fools. Human wisdom without God always ends in moral and spiritual blindness.

In their foolishness, people threw away the true worship of the living, immortal God. Instead, they carved and bowed down to idols made to look like mortal humans, birds, animals, and reptiles. They traded the supreme glory of their Maker for perishable things that rot and die.

Because people insisted on worshiping idols, God gave them over to the shameful lusts of their own hearts. He allowed them to slide into sexual impurity, bringing dishonor upon their own bodies. When people reject God, moral ruin and the loss of self-control naturally follow.

differ.view: God giving sinners over is a judicial sentence where he actively hands them over to the power and ruin of their own sin.
God gives sinners up by withdrawing his restraining grace and allowing their own evil desires to control them.

notes.meaning: Sinners made a terrible trade by giving up the truth about God to follow a lie. They chose to worship and serve created things rather than the Creator who made them. Paul pauses to praise God with an 'Amen,' reminding readers that God alone deserves eternal honor.

Because people turned away from God, he handed them over to shameful and dishonorable passions. Even women turned away from natural sexual relationships as God designed them and chose unnatural ones with other women. Paul points to this distortion as proof of how far humanity had fallen from God's creative order.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern interpreters argue Paul was only condemning exploitative customs like pederasty, or heterosexual people acting against their nature, rather than committed same-sex partnerships.

notes.meaning: In the same way, men abandoned natural relations with women and burned with lust for other men. They committed shameful acts together, breaking God's pattern for marriage and human sexuality. In doing so, they brought upon themselves the painful and destructive consequences of their rebellion.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern interpreters argue Paul was only condemning exploitative customs like pederasty, or heterosexual people acting against their nature, rather than committed same-sex partnerships.

notes.meaning: Since people refused to keep God in their thoughts or acknowledge him as Lord, God gave them over to a corrupted mind. Their ability to tell right from wrong broke down, and their thinking became completely distorted. As a result, they rushed headlong into actions that ought never to be done.

Having lost God's light, society was flooded with every form of evil, greed, and spiteful behavior. People were full of jealousy, murder, fighting, cheating, and cruel intentions. They also became secret gossips, tearing down others behind their backs.

This downward slide led to open slander, hatred of God, and arrogant bullying of others. People boasted of themselves and stayed busy inventing new methods of doing evil. They even broke down the basic order of the home by disobeying their parents.

People lost their moral understanding and threw away their promises whenever it suited them. They showed no natural affection or love for their own families and close relatives. When they saw others hurting, they shut their hearts and showed no pity or mercy.

Even though people know deep down that God's law justly decrees death for such evil deeds, they keep doing them anyway. Worse still, they actively cheer on and praise others who practice these wicked things. Supporting and celebrating sin in others shows how deeply human hearts have rebelled against God.
